summary:
Tatarstan is an autonomous republic within the Russian Federation and stands under the national legal framework, which the Russia record carries in full. The sources consulted for this record identify no Tatarstan-specific statute, court ruling, enforcement action or institutional practice bearing on transgender visitors, and no regional provision that adds to or departs from the national framework.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (version 2.0, June 2025) treats Tatarstan as an ordinary region. The note locates its elevated state-persecution exception outside ordinary regions such as Tatarstan; that exception is the category covering trans people, public LGBT+ advocates and North Caucasus residents likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. The note sets an asylum assessment standard for UK claims rather than describing conditions in the republic.
tangentialFactors:
National enforcement figures for the propaganda and extremism provisions are published as country totals and are not broken down by region, so no Tatarstan-specific case count can be derived from them.

The elevated exception in the Home Office note is defined by category rather than by place. It turns on being transgender, on public advocacy, or on residence in the North Caucasus, and its application to a particular Russian region follows from those categories rather than from any regional law.
localsOnly: No provision specific to Tatarstan affecting transgender residents, whether on identity documents, healthcare, employment, housing or facilities, was identified in the sources consulted. Residents of the republic are subject to the national framework set out in the Russia record.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Tatarstan-specific information was located on police practice, on prosecution of the propaganda or extremism provisions in the republic, on healthcare provision, or on the treatment of transgender people in custody or in regional facilities.

The Home Office assessment is a refugee-status guidance document. It does not measure the frequency of violence, discrimination or official harassment in Tatarstan, and no regional incident data was available to test it.
